THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173 (1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO,
CALL FOR THE RECORDS 1) MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 18/08/2018 PASSED BY THE COURT OF THE ADDL MACT AND PRL. SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND CJM COURT AT BIDAR IN MVC NO.617/2014 AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM
ORAL JUDGMENT
(PER: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)
Captioned appeal is by the claimants, who have lost their minor son hardly aged 12 years.
Feeling aggrieved by the quantum determined and dismissal of the claim petition against the insurance company on the ground that there is a breach of policy conditions, present appeal is filed.
2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellants and learned counsel appearing for respondent - Insurance Company.

Regarding liability 3. The Tribunal has proceeded to fasten liability on the owner of the offending vehicle on the premises that NC: 2024:KHC-K:8243 the rider of the offending motorcycle did not possess driving licence at the time of the accident.

This issue is clearly covered by the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of PAPPU AND OTHERS Vs. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER1 and also the judgment rendered by the Full Bench of this Court in the case NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. YALLAVVA AND ANOTHER.2

entities.text: PAPPU AND OTHERS Vs. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. YALLAVVA AND ANOTHER.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said judgments, it is held that mere breach of policy condition will not absorb the primary liability to satisfy the compensation by the insurer.
Therefore, this finding is perverse and contrary to law laid down by the Apex Court and by the Full Bench of this Court.
This finding deserves reversal.
Accordingly, this Court holds that 2nd respondent - insurance company shall pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the offending bike.
(2018) 3 SCC 208 (2020) 3 KCCR 1469 NC: 2024:KHC-K:8243 Regarding quantum 4.

So far as quantum is concerned, this Court is of the view that global compensation of Rs.5,73,878/- awarded to the parents on account of death of a minor son aged 12 years appears to be on the lower side.

The Coordinate Bench in a reported judgment citing various judgments and provisions of M.V.Act has prepared a chart relating to death of minor children and two distinct Ahmed S/O Shamshuddin And Anr vs Irappa S/O Gundappa And Anr on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144515678/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: tables

are prepared by the Coordinate Bench in the reported judgment, where on account of death of a minor child, the surviving single parent and in case of surviving both the parents is meticulously dealt with at paragraph No.103.
5.
In the case on hand, it is death of minor child survived by both the parents.
Accident is of the year 2014.
The minor child was admittedly aged 12 years.
On account of death of a minor child below 15 years for the year 2014, the amount payable is indicated as Rs.11,16,185/-.

Therefore, this Court is of the view that the parents are globally entitled for a sum of Rs.10,65,305/-as against Rs.Rs.5,73,878/-awarded by the NC: 2024:KHC-K:8243 Tribunal under the head of loss of dependency.
The medical bills amounting to Rs.1,98,878/- is retained.

6. In view of the above, this Court passes the following:
ORDER a) Appeal is allowed in part.
b) Appellants/claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,90,305/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till its realization.

c) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company shall satisfy the award and thereafter,
recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
d) Apportionment shall be made as per the order of the Tribunal.

Sd/-
